subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Concept, Coverage, Method, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and current interaction-design best practices (decision-shape-driven control selection, comparison vs hiding, modal vs inline, sequence ceremony, bulk selection, keyboard alternatives).

cases.scenario: A pricing-plan selector uses a single dropdown listing five plans. Users complain they cannot tell which plan to pick because they have to open the dropdown, read one, close, reopen, and compare from memory.
cases.context: The decision genuinely requires weighing features and price across the plans.
cases.question: What interaction pattern should the agent recommend?
expected_flags: The decision is 'compare' - hidden options in a dropdown defeat it
Use an always-visible comparison pattern (cards/segmented/comparison table)
Hiding options is acceptable only when comparison is not required
Keep the needed comparison context visible while choosing
expected_fix_hints: Replace the dropdown with visible plan cards or a comparison table + single-select
Surface differentiating attributes side by side
absent_signals: Do not keep comparable options hidden in a dropdown
Do not force the user to compare from memory

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: The decision is 'compare' - hidden options in a dropdown defeat it.
Surfaces this expected flag: Use an always-visible comparison pattern (cards/segmented/comparison table).
Surfaces this expected flag: Hiding options is acceptable only when comparison is not required.
Surfaces this expected flag: Keep the needed comparison context visible while choosing.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Replace the dropdown with visible plan cards or a comparison table + single-select.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Surface differentiating attributes side by side.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep comparable options hidden in a dropdown.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not force the user to compare from memory.

cases.scenario: Editing a cell in a data table opens a centered modal that covers the table. Users repeatedly close it to re-check neighboring rows, then reopen it, because the edit depends on the surrounding values.
cases.context: The edit is small and the source context (neighboring rows) matters to the decision.
cases.question: How should the agent change the pattern?
expected_flags: A modal blocks the very context the user needs to decide
Use inline edit (or a non-blocking side panel) so the table stays visible
Choose the pattern from the decision: edit-in-context favors inline over modal
Define commit/cancel/escape behavior for the inline edit
expected_fix_hints: Switch to inline edit with explicit save/cancel, or a docked panel that keeps the table visible
Reserve modals for interactions that genuinely must block the surface
absent_signals: Do not keep a context-blocking modal for an in-context edit
Do not require constant open/close to compare neighbors

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: A modal blocks the very context the user needs to decide.
Surfaces this expected flag: Use inline edit (or a non-blocking side panel) so the table stays visible.
Surfaces this expected flag: Choose the pattern from the decision: edit-in-context favors inline over modal.
Surfaces this expected flag: Define commit/cancel/escape behavior for the inline edit.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Switch to inline edit with explicit save/cancel, or a docked panel that keeps the table visible.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Reserve modals for interactions that genuinely must block the surface.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep a context-blocking modal for an in-context edit.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not require constant open/close to compare neighbors.

cases.scenario: A signup collects name, email, and password but presents them as a 3-step wizard with Next/Back buttons and a progress bar.
cases.context: The three fields are independent and short; there is no branching or long sequence.
cases.question: What should the agent recommend?
expected_flags: A wizard adds ceremony to a task that only needed one form
Collapse to a single form for a short, non-branching set of fields
Reserve steppers/wizards for genuinely long or ordered/branching sequences
The simplest pattern keeping context visible wins
expected_fix_hints: Use one form with all three fields and a single submit
Keep a stepper only if steps are long, ordered, or branch
absent_signals: Do not wrap a 3-field form in a multi-step wizard
Do not add a progress bar to a one-screen task

Surfaces this expected flag: The simplest pattern keeping context visible wins.

cases.scenario: An inbox lets users archive emails only one at a time via a per-row button. Power users archiving dozens of messages find it slow and repetitive.
cases.context: The action is repeated across many rows and users want to act on many at once.
cases.question: How should the agent design the interaction?
expected_flags: The decision shape is 'choose many' / repeated - use multi-select with a contextual action bar
Provide select-all, range select, and clear; favor keyboard-first for repeated actions
Define invalid/partial-action, cancel, and undo behavior for the bulk action
Check the pattern under loading, empty, and permission-limited states
expected_fix_hints: Add row checkboxes + a bulk action bar with archive
Support shift-range select and keyboard shortcuts
absent_signals: Do not keep only a per-row one-at-a-time action for a repeated bulk task
Do not omit select-all / range select

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: The decision shape is 'choose many' / repeated - use multi-select with a contextual action bar.
Surfaces this expected flag: Provide select-all, range select, and clear; favor keyboard-first for repeated actions.
Surfaces this expected flag: Define invalid/partial-action, cancel, and undo behavior for the bulk action.
Surfaces this expected flag: Check the pattern under loading, empty, and permission-limited states.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Add row checkboxes + a bulk action bar with archive.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Support shift-range select and keyboard shortcuts.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep only a per-row one-at-a-time action for a repeated bulk task.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not omit select-all / range select.

cases.scenario: A list relies on swipe-to-delete as the only way to remove an item. Keyboard and desktop-mouse users have no way to delete, and the action is undiscoverable.
cases.context: The product runs on both touch and pointer/keyboard platforms.
cases.question: What is wrong and how should the agent fix it?
expected_flags: A pointer/touch-only gesture must have a keyboard or explicit-control alternative
Add a visible/explicit delete control (overflow menu or button) alongside the swipe
Define escape/cancel and undo for the destructive action
Discoverability: the gesture alone is not a sufficient affordance
expected_fix_hints: Expose an explicit delete affordance plus keyboard support; keep swipe as an accelerator
absent_signals: Do not leave swipe as the only delete path
Do not omit the keyboard/explicit alternative

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: A pointer/touch-only gesture must have a keyboard or explicit-control alternative.
Surfaces this expected flag: Add a visible/explicit delete control (overflow menu or button) alongside the swipe.
Surfaces this expected flag: Define escape/cancel and undo for the destructive action.
Surfaces this expected flag: Discoverability: the gesture alone is not a sufficient affordance.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Expose an explicit delete affordance plus keyboard support; keep swipe as an accelerator.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Offer undo after delete.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not leave swipe as the only delete path.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not omit the keyboard/explicit alternative.

cases.scenario: A PM asks the interaction-patterns owner to define the combobox component's props/variants/slots, audit its ARIA roles, and decide what the loading spinner looks like after selection.
cases.context: The team conflates pattern choice with component API design, accessibility, and feedback staging.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Component props/variants/slots/token contract are design-system-architecture / component-architecture, handed off
ARIA roles and keyboard support are a11y's domain, handed off
The post-selection loading/feedback is interaction-feedback's domain, handed off
Offer the in-scope part: confirming combobox is the right pattern for this decision (large searchable set)
expected_fix_hints: Route API design to design-system-architecture, accessibility to a11y, feedback to interaction-feedback
absent_signals: Do not define the component API
Do not implement the ARIA wiring
Do not design the loading feedback states

_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
